name: Gray hair reversal supplements

lead: Some people take copper, vitamin B12 or other supplements hoping to restore natural hair color. Gray hair has no gray pigment; it results from reduced melanin production at the root, and greying is attributed largely to genetics, with melanocyte stem cell loss thought to trigger it.

Proponents argue that supplying missing nutrients supports pigment production, and greying linked to a deficiency such as B12 may reverse once the cause is resolved. Wikipedia's article on greying states that no special diet, supplement, vitamin or protein has been proven to slow, stop or affect normal greying.

paras: People take over-the-counter supplements or multivitamins marketed for hair color, often after checking for a deficiency with a clinician. Hair grows slowly, so any color change would appear in new growth over months rather than in existing gray strands.

The sources used here do not list supplement-specific harms. Deficiency testing and medical conditions such as thyroid disease are discussed in clinical literature as separate causes of greying, and a clinician can check for them.

angle.text: People take copper, B12 and similar supplements hoping to restore pigment production and bring back natural hair color. Reversal is reported where a deficiency caused the greying; Wikipedia says no supplement has been proven to affect normal greying.

lead: Gray hair reversal supplements are products and nutrients, such as copper and vitamin B12, that some people take hoping to restore natural hair color. Gray hair has no gray pigment; it results from reduced melanin production at the root [1].

Greying is attributed largely to genetics, and melanocyte stem cell loss is thought to trigger it [1]. The Wikipedia article on greying states that no special diet, supplement, vitamin or protein has been proven to slow, stop or affect the process, while noting that greying linked to a deficiency such as B12 may reverse when the cause is resolved [1].
infobox: Loss of melanocyte stem cells, reduced melanin [1]

paras: Genetics is described as nearly the whole determinant of age of onset; a 2016 study of about 6,000 people in five Latin American countries identified IRF4 but found environmental factors accounted for about 70% of cases [1]. Oxidative stress has been proposed as a contributor, though presented as speculative [1]. Conditions such as thyroid deficiency and vitamin B12 deficiency may cause grey hair, and smoking was correlated with premature greying in a 1996 BMJ study [1].

Grey segments caused by stress, chemicals or nutrient deficiency may reverse when the issue resolves, according to cited research including a 2021 paper on greying and life stress [1]. A 2002 letter reported hair regaining color in leukemia patients treated with imatinib, a drug with serious side effects whose mechanism is unknown [1]. A 2020 Nature study in rats found immune overactivity destroyed melanocyte stem cells permanently [1].

No studies found of supplements for reversing age-related gray hair. Related evidence consists of a single 1991 case report linking B12 deficiency to grey hair in a child, as cited in the encyclopedia article [1].
